developers.title: A support button for your docs site.
developers.sub: One script tag. No layout shift. Give it a goal and it hides once the goal is met. Fully configurable.
developers.snippet:
<script>
  window.QuietJar = {
    "site": "qj_your_site_id",
    "currency": "eur",
    "amounts": [3, 5, 10],
    "labels": {
      "headline": "Support this site",
      "body": "Enjoying the docs? Buy us a coffee.",
      "action": "Tip"
    },
    "style": { "color": "#0369a1", "font": "rounded" },
    "close": { "enabled": true, "after": "session" },
    "position": { "corner": "bottom-right" }
  };
</script>
<script src="https://quietjar.com/js/latest/quietjar.js" async></script>

install.title: Install
steps: Copy the snippet and paste it into your page's HTML.
Fill in your site id from the dashboard. If you are logged in on this site, it is already filled in.
Adjust the settings below. Every one of them has a default, so the snippet works as pasted.
install.frameworks: Plain HTML shown here. Astro, Hugo, Docusaurus, and VitePress work the same way: the snippet goes in the layout or in the page.

settings.title: Settings reference
settings.intro: The widget reads its settings from a window.QuietJar object on the page, before the script tag loads. Every setting has a default; site is the only one with a visible consequence when it is missing.
settings.siteNote: Logged in on this site? Your own site id is filled into the snippet above. Your personalized snippet is also on the widget page in the dashboard.

rows.name: site
rows.description: Your public site key from the dashboard. Without it the widget renders, but the checkout cannot take payments.

rows.name: currency
rows.description: ISO 4217 three-letter code, case-insensitive. The bounds and preset amounts follow the currency. An unknown code falls back to eur.

rows.name: goal
rows.description: A goal id from the dashboard. When set, the card renders a progress meter for it.

rows.name: goalReached
rows.description: What the widget does once the goal is reached. Ignored without a goal. Anything else falls back to hide.

options.description: The widget stops rendering, so the page no longer asks.
The widget stays and keeps taking donations, without the bar.
The widget stays and keeps the filled bar.

rows.name: amounts
rows.description: Amounts offered in the checkout, in major units. At most 4 are kept, deduplicated and sorted. Entries that are not finite numbers or sit outside the currency's bounds are dropped; if none survive, the presets are used.

rows.name: labels.headline
rows.description: The button label. When unset, the widget renders as an icon-only pill whose accessible name falls back to "Support this site".

rows.name: labels.body
rows.description: The card body. When set, the widget renders as a card with a headline and an action button instead of a pill button.

rows.name: labels.icon
rows.description: The icon on the button: any text glyph, or piggy for the pig mark. An empty string removes the icon. A value longer than 8 characters falls back to the default.

rows.name: labels.action
rows.description: The card's action button label.

rows.name: labels.close
rows.description: The accessible name of the close control.

rows.name: labels.thanks
rows.description: Shown in the checkout once a tip succeeds.

rows.name: labels.other
rows.description: The label of the free-entry amount option.

rows.name: labels.minimize
rows.description: The accessible name of the control that collapses the checkout.

rows.name: style.color
rows.description: The accent color as a hex value: #rgb, #rgba, #rrggbb or #rrggbbaa. Anything else falls back to the default.

rows.name: style.font
rows.description: The font stack the widget uses. Anything else falls back to rounded.

options.description: The platform's own UI font, such as San Francisco or Segoe UI.
A system serif, such as Georgia or Charter.
A rounded system font, such as SF Pro Rounded. Falls back to the system font where none is installed.
A system monospace font, such as SF Mono or Cascadia Mono.

rows.name: style.css
rows.description: Raw CSS appended after the widget's own stylesheet, for overrides the settings above cannot express.

rows.name: close.enabled
rows.description: Whether the close control visitors can use to dismiss the widget is shown.

rows.name: close.after
rows.description: What a visitor closing the widget does to its visibility. Anything else falls back to session.

options.description: Reappears on the next page load.

rows.name: close.days
rows.description: How many days the widget stays hidden after a visitor closes it. Only used when close.after is days. It must be a whole number of one or more; any other value falls back to 7.

rows.name: donation.hideDays
rows.description: How many days the widget stays hidden after a completed donation, so it does not ask again right away. It follows the same whole-number rule as close.days.

rows.name: position.corner
rows.description: Where the widget floats. Anything else falls back to bottom-right.

options.description: Bottom right corner of the viewport.
Bottom left corner of the viewport.
Top right corner of the viewport.
Top left corner of the viewport.

rows.name: mount.target
rows.description: A CSS selector or element the widget mounts into, inside the page's flow, instead of floating in the fixed corner. Invalid or missing falls back to the corner.

examples.name: amounts
examples.line: amounts: [3, 5, 10] offers three preset buttons in the checkout, shown in the site's currency.

examples.name: close.after
examples.line: close.after: "days" with close.days: 7 hides the widget for a week after a visitor dismisses it.

examples.name: labels.icon
examples.line: labels.icon: "☕" puts a coffee cup on the button. labels.icon: "" removes the icon entirely.

examples.name: position.corner
examples.line: position.corner: "bottom-center" floats the widget at the bottom center of the viewport.

examples.name: mount.target
examples.line: mount.target: "#donate-slot" places the widget inline inside that element instead of the floating corner.

settings.invalid: Nothing fails loudly. Every setting falls back to the default listed above when it is missing or invalid, and unusable amounts entries are dropped rather than shown. The only value with visible consequences when missing is site: the widget renders, but the checkout cannot take payments.

performance.title: Performance
performance.text: Script size: 38.6 kB (11.7 kB gzipped over the wire). Load time: around 40 ms on a cold cache. The button floats in a fixed corner layer, so it displaces nothing on your page: zero layout shift. Stripe's payment code loads only when someone opens the checkout, not on page load.

stepsBack.title: How it steps back
stepsBack.text: After a successful payment, the button enters a quiet state for a while and shows a thank-you instead of asking again. The record lives in the visitor's browser, so nothing is stored on our side and there is no server-side suppression. You pick how long it steps back in the dashboard: 30 days by default. Safari clears browser storage after 7 days without a visit, so a long step-back can end early there. Internally we call it suppression.

items.name: Apple Pay
items.line: Appears on iPhone, iPad, and Mac. One tap with Face ID.

items.name: Google Pay
items.line: Appears in Chrome and on Android. One tap, no forms.

items.name: Cards
items.line: Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Cartes Bancaires. The fallback that always works.

items.name: Link
items.line: Stripe's own wallet. Returning supporters pay without retyping a card.

items.name: iDEAL
items.line: For visitors with a Dutch bank. They pay in their own banking app.

items.name: Local methods
items.line: Bancontact, EPS, Revolut Pay, BLIK, Satispay, Pay by Bank, where available.

goals.title: Goals
goals.text: Give the button a public target and a bar that fills toward it: hosting for the year, the next release, a new microphone. Concrete goals lift the amounts people choose. Set one in the dashboard next to the button's style.

programmatic.title: Open the panel from your own code
programmatic.text: Wire the checkout to your own call to action: the end of an article, a finished download, a tag manager. Call window.QuietJar.open() anywhere on the page and the panel opens right there. It sits next to the widget when that is visible, and centers on the page when it is not. The call always opens, even for visitors the widget stepped back for.

openSource.title: Open source
openSource.text: Every line that runs on your page is public. The widget, the dashboard and the API are open source under the AGPL-3.0 license, so you can read exactly what you are adding to your site before you add it. Found a bug or want a setting we do not have? Open an issue or send a pull request.
